description: This comforting Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known as Adas, is a staple in Middle Eastern cuisine, offering a heartwarming blend of earthy lentils, aromatic spices, and a bright finish of lemon. It is a wonderfully nutritious and satisfying meal, perfect for a cozy evening or a light lunch. Its simple yet profound flavors make it a beloved classic.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Rinse the red lentils thoroughly under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add the minced garlic and diced carrot, cooking for another 3 minutes until fragrant.

instructions.title: Add Spices and Lentils
instructions.text: Stir in the ground cumin and ground turmeric, cooking for 1 minute until aromatic. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils to the pot, stirring to combine them with the vegetables and spices.

instructions.title: Simmer the Soup
instructions.text: Pour in the vegetable broth and water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Achieve Desired Consistency
instructions.text: Once the lentils are cooked, use an immersion blender to partially blend the soup directly in the pot, or carefully transfer about half of the soup to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids). Blend until smooth, then return to the pot. This creates a creamy texture while leaving some whole lentils for chewiness. If the soup is too thick, add a little more water or broth.

instructions.title: Season and Finish
instructions.text: Season the soup with salt and black pepper to taste. The amount will depend on the saltiness of your broth. Stir in the freshly squeezed lemon juice. This is a crucial step that brightens the entire flavor profile of the Adas soup.

instructions.title: Serve Hot
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup into bowls. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro or parsley. Serve immediately with a side of toasted pita bread, lemon wedges, or a drizzle of extra virgin olive oil if desired.

tips: Always rinse lentils thoroughly to remove any debris and excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy.
The fresh lemon juice added at the end is essential for the authentic Lebanese flavor. Do not skip it, as it brightens the earthy notes of the lentils beautifully.
For an extra layer of flavor, you can sauté a small amount of vermicelli pasta until golden brown before adding it with the lentils and liquids.
article:
The aroma of simmering spices and the promise of a hearty meal are hallmarks of Middle Eastern cuisine, and few dishes embody this comfort better than a bowl of Adas. This humble yet incredibly flavourful lentil soup has nourished generations, offering warmth, sustenance, and a taste of home. From bustling souks to quiet family kitchens, its rich history and simple ingredients make it a beloved staple. If you’re seeking a dish that’s both deeply satisfying and remarkably easy to prepare, then Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is about to become your new favourite.

## What is Lebanese Red Lentil Soup (Adas)?

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup, known affectionately as Adas, is a quintessential dish in Middle Eastern culinary traditions, particularly cherished in Lebanon. It's a vibrant, often creamy, and intensely flavourful soup made primarily from red lentils. Unlike some other lentil soups that might be thick with vegetables or meat, Adas typically focuses on the pure, earthy goodness of the lentils themselves, brightened by a generous squeeze of lemon and often a hint of cumin.

Its distinct orange-red hue comes from the lentils and sometimes a touch of turmeric. Adas is more than just a soup; it’s a symbol of comfort, a budget-friendly meal, and a nutritious powerhouse, frequently served during colder months, as a light lunch, or as an appetizer. Its simplicity belies a depth of flavour that makes it incredibly satisfying, proving that the most comforting foods are often made from the most basic ingredients.

## Ingredients for Lebanese Red Lentil Soup

Creating an authentic Lebanese Red Lentil Soup requires a handful of accessible, everyday ingredients. The beauty of Adas lies in how these simple components combine to form such a rich and complex flavour profile.

Here’s what you’ll need:

*   **Red Lentils:** The star of the show. These quick-cooking lentils break down easily, creating the soup's characteristic creamy texture. Ensure they are rinsed thoroughly before use.
*   **Olive Oil:** A foundational ingredient in Lebanese cooking, used for sautéing the aromatics and often drizzled generously over the finished soup for flavour and richness.
*   **Onion & Garlic:** The aromatic backbone. Sautéing these until fragrant builds a crucial flavour base for the soup.
*   **Carrots (Optional but Recommended):** While not strictly traditional in every variation, a chopped carrot adds a touch of sweetness, extra nutrients, and contributes to the soup's appealing colour.
*   **Cumin:** This spice is non-negotiable for Adas. Its warm, earthy notes perfectly complement the lentils.
*   **Turmeric (Optional):** A pinch of turmeric can enhance the soup's golden colour and add a subtle, earthy undertone.
*   **Vegetable Broth or Water:** The liquid base. Broth will add more depth of flavour, but water works perfectly well, especially with the other strong flavours.
*   **Fresh Lemon Juice:** Crucial for brightening the soup and cutting through the richness of the lentils. It adds a zesty tang that elevates the entire dish.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To season the soup to perfection.
*   **Fresh Herbs (e.g., Parsley or Mint):** For garnish, adding a burst of freshness and a touch of vibrant green.

## How to Make Lebanese Red Lentil Soup: Step-by-Step

Making Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a straightforward process, perfect for cooks of all skill levels. Follow these steps for a delicious bowl of Adas:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Start by rinsing your red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any debris or starch. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat a generous drizzle of olive oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add the minced garlic and chopped carrots (if using), and cook for another 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
3.  **Add Lentils & Spices:** Stir in the rinsed lentils, cumin, and turmeric (if using). Sauté for about a minute, allowing the spices to toast slightly and release their aromas.
4.  **Pour in Liquid:** Pour in the vegetable broth or water. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and let it simmer.
5.  **Cook Until Tender:** Allow the soup to simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the red lentils are completely tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
6.  **Blend (Optional):** For a smoother, creamier texture, you can use an immersion blender to partially or fully blend the soup directly in the pot. Alternatively, scoop a portion into a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot. If you prefer a chunkier soup, simply mash some of the lentils with the back of a spoon.
7.  **Season and Finish:** Stir in the fresh lemon juice, salt, and black pepper to taste. Adjust seasoning as needed. If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until you reach your desired consistency.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Lebanese Red Lentil Soup into bowls.

## Tips for the Best Adas Soup

While simple, a few key tips can elevate your Lebanese Red Lentil Soup from good to truly exceptional:

*   **Rinse Your Lentils:** Don't skip this step! Rinsing removes impurities and excess starch, resulting in a cleaner-tasting soup.
*   **Sauté Well:** Take your time sautéing the onions and garlic until they are soft and fragrant. This foundational step builds crucial flavour.
*   **Fresh Lemon is Key:** Bottled lemon juice simply doesn't compare to the brightness and zing of fresh lemon. It's the indispensable ingredient that truly defines Adas.
*   **Adjust Consistency:** Red lentils absorb a lot of liquid. Feel free to add more hot water or broth towards the end of cooking or when reheating if the soup becomes too thick for your liking.
*   **Taste and Adjust:** Seasoning is personal. Taste your soup throughout the cooking process and adjust salt, pepper, and lemon juice until it's perfect for your palate.
*   **Let it Rest:** Like many soups, the flavours of Adas deepen and meld beautifully if allowed to rest for 10-15 minutes before serving, or even better, overnight.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is a wonderfully versatile dish that can be enjoyed in various ways. It's often served as a light meal on its own, but it also pairs beautifully with other Middle Eastern staples.

Traditional accompaniments include:

*   **Pita Bread:** Essential for scooping up every last drop of the delicious soup. Warm pita bread, fresh or toasted, is a must.
*   **Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** A final drizzle of good quality olive oil over each bowl adds a layer of richness and aromatic depth.
*   **Fresh Herbs:** A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley or mint provides a refreshing contrast and vibrant colour.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** Always serve with extra lemon wedges on the side, allowing each diner to add more zest to their liking.
*   **Pickles (Mkhalal):** Middle Eastern pickles, such as turnip or cucumber pickles, offer a tangy counterpoint to the soup's richness.
*   **Side Salad:** A simple green salad or a traditional Fattoush salad provides a refreshing crunch and balances the meal.
*   **Fried Pita Chips/Croutons:** For added texture, some people enjoy topping their Adas with crispy fried pita chips or simple croutons.

## Storage and Reheating Tips

One of the great things about Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is how well it stores and reheats, making it an excellent meal prep option.

*   **Refrigeration:** Store leftover Adas in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
*   **Freezing:** This soup freezes beautifully. Allow it to cool completely, then transfer it to freezer-safe containers or bags. It can be frozen for up to 3 months. Thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.
*   **Reheating:** Reheat gently on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, or in the microwave. The soup will likely thicken in the fridge, so you may need to add a splash of water or vegetable broth to thin it to your desired consistency. Always taste and adjust seasonings, especially adding a fresh squeeze of lemon juice, after reheating for the best flavour.

## Variations and Dietary Adaptations

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is naturally wholesome and adaptable, catering to various dietary needs and preferences.

*   **Spicier Kick:** For those who enjoy a bit of heat, a pinch of cayenne pepper or a finely minced fresh green chili can be added along with the other spices.
*   **Herb Variations:** While parsley is common, fresh cilantro or mint can also be used as a garnish, offering different aromatic profiles.
*   **Greens Boost:** Stir in a handful of fresh spinach or Swiss chard during the last 5 minutes of cooking for added nutrients and a touch of green.
*   **Smoky Notes:** A hint of smoked paprika can lend a subtle smoky depth to the soup.
*   **Vegetarian and Vegan:** Adas is inherently vegetarian and vegan, provided you use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth. It's a fantastic plant-based protein source.
*   **Gluten-Free:** The recipe is naturally gluten-free, but if serving with bread, ensure you choose a gluten-free option for those with sensitivities.
*   **Creamier Texture:** For an even richer, creamier soup, some recipes incorporate a small amount of rice (often short-grain) cooked along with the lentils. This adds body and a velvety texture.

Lebanese Red Lentil Soup is more than just a meal; it's an experience of comfort, flavour, and tradition. Its simplicity, combined with its nourishing qualities and incredible taste, makes it a timeless classic in Middle Eastern cuisine. Whether you're seeking a healthy weeknight dinner or a comforting bowl to warm you from the inside out, Adas is a culinary journey well worth taking.
